misconceptions.text: Splits the polygon into $n$ triangles instead of $n - 2$, e.g. hexagon angle sum $= 6 \times 180^\circ = 1080^\circ$.
misconceptions.correction: Triangles drawn from one vertex: a hexagon gives 4 triangles, so the sum is $(6 - 2) \times 180^\circ = 720^\circ$. Check with a square: $(4 - 2) \times 180^\circ = 360^\circ$, which is correct.

misconceptions.text: Gives $\frac{360^\circ}{n}$ as the interior angle of a regular polygon, e.g. says each interior angle of a regular octagon is $360^\circ \div 8 = 45^\circ$.
misconceptions.correction: $\frac{360^\circ}{n}$ is the exterior angle. Interior $= 180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ$. Each interior angle of a regular polygon with 5 or more sides is obtuse.

misconceptions.text: Finds the number of sides by dividing $360^\circ$ by the interior angle, e.g. interior angle $140^\circ$ gives $n = 360 \div 140 \approx 2.6$.
misconceptions.correction: Divide $360^\circ$ by the exterior angle: exterior $= 180^\circ - 140^\circ = 40^\circ$, so $n = 360 \div 40 = 9$.

misconceptions.text: Uses the regular-polygon method on an irregular polygon, e.g. finds a missing angle of an irregular hexagon as $720^\circ \div 6 = 120^\circ$.
misconceptions.correction: Only a regular polygon has equal angles. For an irregular polygon, subtract the known angles from the angle sum: missing angle $= 720^\circ - (\text{sum of the other five})$.
